ai.text:
The European Parliament approved a regulation, by 530 votes in favour, 125 against and 12 abstentions, that changes several existing EU rules to make it easier for Europe to prepare its defence and for its defence industry to grow. It is part of a wider package of defence readiness measures and extends existing provisions from defence and non-defence laws to remove obstacles to defence investment.

The measure adjusts the European Defence Fund so that it helps the EU reach defence readiness by 2030, strengthening its strategic autonomy and resilience against a wide range of threats, including hybrid operations and the risk of armed aggression. The Fund is also meant to make the EU's defence industrial base more resilient, including by developing technologies that save energy and reduce reliance on outside suppliers for critical raw materials, and to encourage cooperation that matches the defence priorities agreed by Member States.

Paperwork for taking part in the Fund is to be reduced and procedures simplified. Small and medium-sized businesses and small mid-cap companies, especially those working across borders, should have fair access to funding calls, and the application and evaluation steps for calls involving them must be much shorter and simpler.

The Fund can also support disruptive defence technologies and research carried out by small and medium-sized businesses. Each proposal is judged on its contribution to excellence in defence, meaning its results must offer clear advantages over existing products or technologies, and on the quality and efficiency of how it would be carried out. Depending on the specific call, proposals may also be assessed on innovation, competitiveness, reducing dependence on non-EU sources, cross-border cooperation, efficiency over a product's life, further integration of the European defence industry, and meeting the needs of countries most exposed to conventional military threats.

Projects linked to permanent structured cooperation or to a structure for European armament programmes can receive a funding rate 10 percentage points higher. Finally, testing carried out in Ukraine, an EU candidate country, will be eligible for Fund support to strengthen cooperation with Ukrainian organisations.
